sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 39 (check 38), Internal Quality Checks row 39 (no annotation), Deterministic Checks A5 check-batched-independence-wording.py
evidence: All three scored prompts tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and to keep going after a failure, and none tells it to stop at the first failure. functional/prompt.md:59-61 says 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion.' Line 29 says 'Two failed attempts at the same control fail that criterion; continue.' Lines 9 and 24-25 say 'that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion' and 'Never carry a verdict across criteria'. polish/prompt.md:20-28 has an 'Independent scoring' section: 'One failed criterion does not zero the others ... mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion; return a verdict for all of them. The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule.' visual/prompt.md:38-43 has the same section, with the 0 anchor used in place of a fail. A grep for 'stop at', 'first fail', 'stop on' and 'abort' finds no stop-on-first-failure wording in tests/scored or app_context.md. The wording matches or exceeds the template's (the template functional prompt line 68; polish and visual have the same 'Independent scoring' sections). Functional also runs with mode='individual' (functional/judge.toml:10), so each criterion gets its own judge session. That structurally stops one miss from zeroing the rest. The gates (render and constraints, aggregation all_pass) are exempt. Adversarial check: in a broken app that fails one functional criterion (for example a missing mention), every other criterion still gets a verdict, because the per-criterion session is told to report and move on. The only all-or-nothing rule is the in-dimension browser gate, which is scoped to dead apps. That is the intended behaviour, not a cascade on a single miss. A conforming app cannot be zeroed by an unrelated miss. Residual note, outside this row's wording scope: the functional criteria share one database in order, so a defective app's leftover state could in principle affect later criteria. The prompt tells each session to judge against the state that earlier criteria left. Evidence is static wording only. The deterministic checker was not executed, and no configured judge run exists for these bytes (per the raw-evidence-index scope), so independence has not been observed at runtime.
